 Koki Watanabe 
 Kumamoto Masters: Watanabe Wins Thriller
 Saturday, November 14, 2026
 TEXT BY BWF STAFF | BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Koki Watanabe reached his second final of the year with a come-from-behind effort against Kunlavut Vitidsarn at the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026.
 Incidentally, Watanabe’s only other final this year was also on home soil – at the DAIHATSU Japan Open in July. The home hope trailed in the second half of the decider, with Vitidsarn taking a three-point lead at 18-15, but Watanabe was tenacious and saved one match point before converting his own second opportunity, 14-21 21-11 23-21.
 In the final, Watanabe takes on Lakshya Sen , who made his second straight final. Sen, who won the HYLO Open a fortnight ago, got his first win over Alwi Farhan in three matches, 21-12 15-21 21-11.
 Both Sen and Watanabe are still in contention for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026, which will be decided at next week’s Hong Kong Open.
 “It feels very good to play here, last time I was in the semifinals, so it’s a better result this time. Tomorrow I will play with a free mindset, and I won’t be thinking of the result,” said Sen.
 In women’s singles, Akane Yamaguchi made her 11 th final of the season after semifinal opponent Chen Yu Fei retired due to a foot injury. Yamaguchi has won three out of 10 finals, but will fancy her chances of a fourth title as her nemesis An Se Young isn’t competing in Japan.
 Instead, she will take on Wang Zhi Yi , who beat Tomoka Miyazaki 21-10 21-15. Yamaguchi has won their last four encounters.
 Men’s doubles saw Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King do their compatriots Aaron Chia/Soh Wooi Yik a favour as they beat Denmark’s Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard. Chia/Soh and Lundgaard/Vestergaard are in a tight race to the World Tour Finals, with the Danes slightly ahead at the moment.
 What They Said 
 “My foot injury hasn’t completely healed, so I approached this tournament mainly to see how it would respond under match conditions. After playing three games, I felt my reactions and hand speed were fine, but physically my foot wasn’t able to sustain the intensity. Rather than risk making the injury worse, I made the decision to retire.” – Chen Yu Fei
 “I could not control the shuttle, I was not good enough. Credit to my opponent. He controlled me and the shuttle. It’s okay, I feel very happy. This time I came to the semifinals, so I’m happy I could play better than before.” – Kunlavut Vitidsarn
 “Congrats to Lakshya, he played well today. He was confident as he’d won HYLO Open. He was aggressive and his smashes were very strong. I don’t know what went wrong. I lost confidence in the first game after I was service-faulted on the flick serve.” – Alwi Farhan
